title: Trial technical onramp lab journal
content:
Purpose: quick, operational lab journal to capture the trial onramp for AcmeCorp (internal POC). Not a final runbook — this is the gritty day-by-day notes, decisions, and temporary workarounds from the field lab. Use to populate the canonical playbook after ship.

Scope / audience:
- Solutions Engineering + Customer SREs + Acme dev lead (Anya).
- Focus: get a minimum viable dedicated deployment (4x A10g equiv) running the demo prompt set, validate latency SLOs, and collect token-cost profile.

High-level acceptance criteria (minimal):
- Baseline throughput: 35 rps sustained 1k-token window with p50 < 120ms for generation step (excluding network RTT).
- End-to-end demo sequence completes under 2s in 95% of runs.
- Metrics pipeline (Prometheus -> Grafana) receives KV-cache hit metric and per-model token counters within first day.
- Customer data never leaves their VPC for testing (private control plane integration validated).

Initial assumptions and constraints (found in kickoff):
- Customer will provide a 3-node test cluster (hooked to our Private control plane) by 11/04.
- Network egress is limited to specific IP ranges; we need whitelist for debug agent.
- Model variant chosen: gpt-redwood-7b-q4f16 (fast quantized path). Fallback: gpt-redwood-13b-q4f16.
- No persistent storage allowed outside cluster (so prefix caching must use in-memory KV only).

Day-by-day lab journal (key entries):
2025-11-03 — pre-lab checklist
- Confirmed VPC peering handshake (net ops). Whitelist request filed: NET-PR-332.
- Uploaded quickstart manifests to customer S3 staging (s3://acme-poc/staging) — note: we used a temporary token.
- Copied our local dev image tag: redwood/poc-runner:2025-11-03a
Open question: Are customer1's GPUs actually A10g or A100? Console shows a custom instance; DM to infra to clarify.

2025-11-04 — day 0: cluster health + bootstrap
- Cluster nodes provisioned (3x). One node had missing NVLINK driver -> patched by infra (driver-524b). Bootstrapped runtime with our private-agent.
- Observability: Prometheus job registered but scrape timeout default was 10s -> bumped to 30s in prometheus.yml.
- First inference container started. Memory OOM on largest checkpoint load (13B fallback). Decision: load only 7B by default; 13B reserved for canary.
Action items: @Daniel to add autoscaler min=2 / max=8 suggestion to proposal doc.

2025-11-05 — performance tuning
- Enabled batched decode (batch size 4) and KV-prefetch = on. Measured token generation p50 reduced from 160ms -> 110ms.
- Discovered prefix cache not populated because client sending ephemeral prompt ids. Added request header x-acme-session to client to stable session id.
- Grafana panel for kv_cache_hits created (panel id: acme-kv-01). Hooked to alert rule: alert if hit_rate < 5% for 10m.
Risk noted: If client continues ephemeral ids, cache benefit disappears; coordinate with Acme devs to persist session header.

2025-11-06 — failure mode and fallback path
- Simulated degraded node (killed one GPU instance). Smart routing triggered fallback to 13B variant but 13B had longer cold-starts -> timed out for some requests.
- Implemented temporary policy: when node count < 2, prefer 7B but reduce batch size to 1 to keep latency.
- Added a circuit-breaker metric: model_cold_start_count.

2025-11-07 — security & compliance check
- KMS integration test passed with customer key alias. Caveat: rotation requires re-synchronizing runtime tokens. Put in follow-up: SE-ops runbook step to rotate keys during maintenance window.
- Audit logging: confirmed request ids flow to customer audit log endpoint. Confirmed PII masking config turned on (PII_MASK_LEVEL=strict) per contract.

Key decisions and rationale (to be folded into final playbook):
- Default onramp model = 7B quantized: consistent latency and significantly lower memory -> lowers flakiness in trial.
- Use session header for cacheability; require customer to add this minimal change for production.
- Autoscaler conservative defaults to avoid repeated cold-start cascades.

Task tracker (short):
- TASK-1: Update proposal with autoscaler min/max (owner: Daniel, due: 2025-11-08)
- TASK-2: Add session header sample snippets to quickstart (owner: Priya, due: 2025-11-06) — STATUS: done
- TASK-3: Create Grafana dashboard export and share with Acme (owner: Lucia, due: 2025-11-09)
- TASK-4: Document KMS rotate procedure in ops playbook (owner: Samir, due: 2025-11-12)
- TASK-5: Follow-up call with Acme devs to discuss ephemeral ids (owner: Maya, due: 2025-11-10)

Temporary troubleshooting snippets (to copy to final guide):
- force a cold-start on node: kubectl scale --replicas=0 deployment/redwood-runtime && sleep 10 && kubectl scale --replicas=3 deployment/redwood-runtime
- tail logs for kv cache activity: kubectl logs -l app=redwood-runtime -c runtime | grep "kv-cache"
- check model memory: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free --format=csv

Known risks / mitigation
- Risk: client behavior prevents cache hits -> mitigation: require session header; add SDK shim to auto-generate stable session id.
- Risk: 13B cold-start latency -> mitigation: warm pool and preferred fallback to 7B; schedule canary windows off-peak.
- Risk: network egress rules block debugging -> mitigation: pre-approve debug IPs and use ephemeral bastion.

Outstanding questions
- Does Acme accept temporary SSH bastion for the diagnostics window? (status: pending — action: Maya to confirm on 11/10)
- Are there regulatory constraints on metrics retention beyond 30 days? If yes, we need to prune event payloads (Samir to coordinate with legal).

Customer-facing demo plan (short script):
- Step 1: Walkthrough of console: show per-route token counters + latency heatmap.
- Step 2: Run the demo prompt set (5 queries): show KV-cache hit increase on repeated prompts.
- Step 3: Trigger induced node failover to demonstrate graceful fallback.
- Step 4: Show cost map and token breakdown for a sample session.
Notes: Keep demo under 20 minutes. Call out that production quantization choices can change latency/quality trade-offs.

Retro notes for the team (less formal):
- Need a smaller set of command snippets in a 1-page diagnostics cheat sheet.
- Make the session header requirement visible in the quickstart (not buried).
- Consider adding a lightweight SDK shim in JS + Python that auto-manages session ids and exponential backoff.

Next steps before wrap (owner tags):
- Daniel: update proposal and push to Confluence (due 11/08)
- Priya: finalize quickstart + sample app zip (done)
- Lucia: export dashboard + share link (due 11/09)
- Samir: draft KMS rotate step in SE-ops playbook (due 11/12)
- Maya: confirm bastion permission and schedule demo (due 11/10)

Sign-off checklist (for final handoff):
- [ ] Metrics ingestion validated
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified (latency/throughput)
- [ ] Security sign-off (KMS/audit) obtained
- [ ] Customer demo scheduled and slide deck prepared

Quick references (internal):
- Quickstart repo: github.com/redwood-inference/poc-scripts (branch: acme-trial)
- Prometheus job: acme-poc/scrape-config
- Jira epic: ENG-4821

(End of lab journal)
